text:
[h1] F*** THIS GAME [/h1]

[h3] My History [/h3]
Now, I've been on this game for a good length of time and then some (been playing on and off since the demo for the Xbox 360 was released). I've grown to playing this game too d*** much for my own good, as well as HALO: The Master Chief Collection, and I title these two games as my all-time "favorites". I put "favorites" in quotes because when it comes to these games, I have played them way more than any other game. Unfortunately, both of these titles piss me the f*** off to no avail and since this is the Review Section for Left 4 Dead 2, I'ma give my honest input.

[h3] The Pros [/h3]
One major benefit of this game is the fact that it is very easy to pick up and play. Another good for it is it is not a hardware demanding title to run on. This game can run on your grandma's toaster oven and as far as I'm aware, it is generally bug-free (probably due to all the patches the game has gone through and updates the game has received). Some other good, is that the characters are enjoyable and while the story is not in your face and not really obvious, there are clues about the story scattered out throughout the game in the form of writings on the saferoom/alley walls from previous survivors and the such. The Developer Commentary mode (found in the 'Extras' menu on the Main Menu screen) is also nothing short of interesting and really good for those who are interested in the Behind-The-Scenes stuff of the game, which I used to play way too much of back on the Xbox 360... Another thing that I like about the game is that climbing the skill-hill is very a smooth experience (assuming you’re actively trying to learn the game) and with the right amount of practice, the hardest tricks in the game can be done with relative ease. Hell, at this point, all I play is Expert because any difficulty less is too easy for me. The last good I will be referring to is the fact that the game has built-in Mod support. Now me personally, I couldn’t give a s*** about mods, considering I play almost vanilla every-time I play. Really, the only mod that I currently use is a mod that turns the crosshair into a small, white dot (I mainly used this for Tier 1 weaponry when I first downloaded it, and btw, Tier 1 weaponry main REPRESENT lol)… There are some other good things about the game, but I ain't here to talk kindly on this piece of dogs***, I'm here to take a fat steamin' turd on it.

[h3] The Cons [/h3]
I genuinely only have one complaint with this game: let me introduce to you possibly the worst idea of an enemy ever introduced into a video game that is reliant on teamwork since f****** EVER: The Smoker. Now, I'm not a violent person and I don't want to wish harm upon anyone, but I seriously hope whoever made this Special Infected got fired from making anymore video game decisions for the rest of their miserable lives and then got beaten horrifically with a butter sock while strapped down to a table... Seriously, this zombie is an ABOMINATION... This motherf***** will snipe you with his tongue and when he has constricted you, he will F*** YOU UP... On Expert, this zombie is a tumor to this game, as 90% of the time, he will corner bomb you the second you take 5ft away from your teammates and once this motherf***** has you, he will somehow INSTANTLY constrict you. I cannot tell you how many times this zombie has timed a tangle on me and while I was falling from a jump, because of where it attacked from, I would get instantly constricted... What makes this c***sucker worse is the fact that, like the Jockey zombie, his audio cues are beyond broken as f***. Half the time (nah scratch that, MOST the time, especially on Expert), this motherf***** is as silent as a mouse and you will NOT hear his music OR audio cues. Combine that with his insanely fast attack speed, damage output, and the fact this motherf***** has the most inconsistent health bar I've ever seen (sometimes you can one tap him, other times you can't for some diddly f*** reason), he is honestly the single worst thing about this game, PERIOD... Oh, and I forgot to mention: not only is he one of the most common to spawn of the Special Infected (meaning you can actually encounter TWO or THREE of these f****** in a row in a REGULAR campaign), but they are also the single HARDEST Special Infected to counter in the entire game... Seriously Valve, F*** YOU for implementing this actual HELLSPAWN unto this game. I truly (and with the upmost sincerity) hope Left 4 Dead 3 never sees the light of f****** day because ya'll had the AUDACITY to add this ONE MOTHERF****** ZOMBIE into a video game... 
[End rant]

[h3] The Conclusion [/h3]
And really that's my review. If you're going to play this game, play this s*** on Advanced or below difficulty, because the AI Infected will cheat like a b**** on Expert. 
Thanks for reading!

Left 4 Dead 2: Where the Real Special Infected Are Your Teammates


Ah, Left 4 Dead 2 – a game where teamwork is essential… if by "teamwork," you mean getting betrayed harder than a horror movie side character.

Here’s how it goes: You’re deep into a campaign, barely holding on, when suddenly a random player joins mid-game.
Great, right? More firepower! Except – plot twist – this guy isn’t here to help. No, he’s here to pull off the greatest Among Us betrayal of all time. Shot in the back. Incapacitated. And while you're lying there, watching your life bar drain, you see it: A kick vote.

The best part? Your teammates accept it instantly, because their brain registers "vote" and thinks, "Yes, democracy! Must click YES!" Congratulations, you’ve been eliminated from your own game faster than a Boomer popping at a frat party.

And speaking of Boomers, let’s talk about the actual infected. You think the Jockey is bad? Try getting piggybacked by a teammate into a Witch. Think a Charger is deadly? That’s cute—wait until a random joins, shoots you in the kneecap, and leaves you for dead while the actual Charger politely watches from the sidelines, impressed. And Smokers? Oh, don’t worry, you’ll still get dragged across the map—it just won’t be by an infected, but by a teammate voting you out after they walked into a Tank’s fists like it’s a trust fall exercise.

But wait, there’s more! My personal highlight: I once had my username in Persian script. That was all it took.
Instantly, I became the prime target for teamkills and some of the most spectacularly dumb racism I’ve ever seen. News flash, folks: Not every foreign script means whatever your tiny brain thinks it means. But sure, please keep screaming slurs while you get pounced by a Hunter. Priorities.

Final Verdict: If you enjoy survival horror, but wish the real horror came from the people you’re supposed to trust, Left 4 Dead 2 is the perfect game for you. Play at your own risk. Or better yet, just queue as a Special Infected – at least then, betrayal is expected.

The game also comes with a DLC, which includes the following items:

1. A Toxic Community: Mistakes are rarely forgiven. Unless you’re playing with friends, be prepared to face harsh criticism, often from younger players. The game’s multiplayer is largely populated by school-aged players who don’t hold back.


2. Disruptive Adults: It’s not just the kids causing chaos—some adults blast music through their microphones, assuming everyone else shares their taste. Spoiler: they don’t.


3. Frequent AFKs: Teamwork can fall apart when a teammate goes inactive, whether they’re brewing tea, taking a smoke break, or simply wandering off mid-game. And yes, it often happens right after you’ve generously used your first aid kit on them.


4. Team Abandonment: Lone wolves running off to the far corners of the map, only to be overwhelmed by infected, are a common sight. They’re quick to flood the chat with colorful language before rage-quitting the game.


5. Difficulty Disputes: Some players join games on "Expert" difficulty only to demand a downgrade. If their request is denied, they might sabotage the team before leaving the server entirely.


6. Vote Kicks: Occasionally, you’ll encounter players who inexplicably start a vote to kick you from the game. When you ask why? Crickets.



The Verdict: Despite the chaotic community, Left 4 Dead 2 remains a phenomenal experience. The graphics are a significant step up from the first game, the mechanics feel more polished, and there’s a greater variety of weapons and infected to enjoy. However, surviving the online experience without a calming remedy might be just as challenging as surviving the zombie apocalypse itself.

text:
What can I say about this game that hasn't been said already? Is it a great game? Absolutely, tons of fun guaranteed with your friends. You will laugh, scream, get angry and rage all in a single session—I promise.
I first played left4dead 2 back in 2011,if memory serves me right, 13 years have passed and I continue playing it, not as much as before though . Over the years I quitted the game, then downloaded it again to revive old memories, then uninstalled it again cause I felt it was taking so much of my time, but I always came back. It's some kind of toxic relationship, but I finally learned to live with that.
It can get very frustrating if you keep losing over and over, to the point that it can ruin your whole day, don't let it take control of your emotions, if you want to play it, play it cause you want to have some fun not because you want to win every single match, that's all.
Pros:
-Several official campaigns
-Dozens of excellent custom campaigns on the workshop(My favorite one being Big Wat)
-Lots of workshop content(items,skins,animations,etc), just don't download too many of them or you will end up playing a completely different game
-Multiple game modes(versus,mutations, scavenge,survival)
-Once bought, you don't need to spend any more money on the game to get the full experience, therefore the only way to get better as a survivor or infected is by playing
-If you feel like going competitive or step up your game, try zonemod or center
Cons:
-There's a high chance that you get kicked out of the game by the other players if you keep screwing up(specially on versus). Even I get kicked out most of the times and I have 2700 hours at this point, don't dwell on it too much
-Trolls(people who don't take the game too seriously). I personally don't really mind them that much, I mean I am one of those sometimes when I want to relax and have some fun in vanilla
-Hackers. Pretty common, but it's kinda funny seeing them flying around or moving as fast as flash by the map. A piece of advice: don’t do it unless you want a VAC ban featured on your Steam profile
-Bugs. Tank spawning earlier for a team, getting insta-killed if the charger that's carrying you gets killed in the air, getting killed in the refuge cause one of the infected did the door bug and so on. You'll get use to them
Rating:9/10
Totally worth playing. If you ever need a teammate, count me in!

text:
15yrs later and Left 4 Dead 2 is still a very fun cooperative multiplayer zombie game. Its always nice to get off from a long day at work and to quickly find a match going. The various modes, especially the Versus mode, still holds up. There usually always a game going on or a lobby being started. You can find a match or lobby within 10 seconds of booting up. The dopamine hit after you setup a nice insta kill with the Charger is amazing! There very few coop games like L4D2 that still hold up.

But whats not nice is the in-game "community" and the constant DDOS attacks on the servers that seem to happen every two months nowadays. Saw a comment the other day that said the L4D2 community is stuck in the 2009 Call of Duty online era and this is very much true. Constant instant kicks from sessions for newer players and players who make simple mistakes while in game. The use of racism is treat as the norm and if you make it known you're not ok with being a terrible Human being, you're in the wrong and will be kicked. I recommend not playing this when a small kid is in the room or at the least turn the option to see sprays off as there are many players who have sprays that feature pornographic images. And not sure when it started but since last year, the servers have been under attack for what seems like every month or so by hackers. Valve puts out patches when they can but the game is old and ripe for new hacker exploits.

Despite most of my review focusing on the negative of the community, the game is still very fun to play with friends when there no issues.

text:
This game saved my life.

I am 42.

My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.

When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.

After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.

Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.

After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.

Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.

I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.

Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.

Thank you
